findings.element: Status filter - reachable only via the "Add filter" menu in the filter bar
findings.finding: The only control that can filter to a specific status is hidden inside the Add filter menu, while the always-visible tab row offers just five coarse groups.
findings.user_impact: A user who arrives from the Dashboard on one specific status (e.g. one of the several failure statuses inside Needs attention) cannot narrow to it without discovering a nested menu, so they work through a mixed group list instead - the same pattern that produced ~0 dropdown clicks against ~986 tab clicks in Summaries (KF-7).
findings.suggested_fix: Render the Status chip in the filter bar by default with its current value shown, rather than requiring it to be added from the Add filter menu.

evidence.action: Opened the "Add filter" menu in the filter bar and added Status, then opened the resulting Status panel
evidence.observed: Status is one of the Add filter menu options and only exists as a filter chip after being added; the menu then offers Type, Amount, Customer. The Status panel lists 19 statuses in 5 groups - the only precise status path on the screen.

findings.element: Segmented status tab row + Status filter chip (two controls, one dimension)
findings.finding: Two independent controls filter status with no visible precedence, and the documented mitigation (a contradicting tab reads 0) only hides the empty result - it never tells the user the Status chip is what emptied the tab.
findings.user_impact: A user with a Status chip applied reads "Successful 0" as "I have no successful transactions" rather than "my other status filter excludes them", and stops or re-syncs rows that are already fine.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the tab row precedence over the chip and surface the conflict inline - when a Status chip narrows the tabs, label the tab row "counts limited by Status: <value>" with a one-click clear.

evidence.action: Applied a Status chip value (picked, Apply reached) and then read the segmented tab row's selection and counts in the recon record
evidence.observed: The tab row carries its own independent selection and one fixed set of counts - All 31 with the five groups summing to exactly 31 - i.e. the unfiltered total; nothing in the record shows the tab row reflecting, naming, or being reset by the chip's value.

findings.finding: The All tab promises 31 transactions but the list renders 25, and every other tab's count matches its rows exactly - so 6 transactions are counted but not reachable.
findings.user_impact: A user auditing "everything" trusts the 31 on the tab, sees 25 rows, and cannot tell whether the remaining 6 are hidden, filtered, or on an unreachable page - the flagged row they came for may be among them.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the All tab's count describe the set the user can actually reach on this screen, or show an explicit "showing 25 of 31" line next to the list.

evidence.action: Clicked each segmented tab in turn and compared its count label to the number of rows rendered
evidence.observed: All 31 -> 25 rows, while Needs attention 8 -> 8, Ready to sync 7 -> 7, In progress 6 -> 6, Successful 8 -> 8, Deleted 2 -> 2. Only the All tab disagrees with its own count.

findings.element: Date range, Platform, Add filter and Status chips in the filter bar
findings.finding: Clicking a filter chip a second time does not close its panel, so the chip reads as a toggle but does not behave as one.
findings.user_impact: A user who opens the wrong filter has no obvious way to back out - they click the chip again, the panel stays put over the content, and they are left guessing whether an unwanted value was committed.
findings.suggested_fix: Make a second click on the chip trigger close its own panel (and dismiss on outside click / Esc), so the chip behaves as the toggle it looks like.

evidence.action: Clicked each filter chip trigger a second time while its panel was open
evidence.observed: All four panels recorded "second toggle: panel stayed open" - the trigger remained visible and clickable but did not dismiss the panel.

gaps: Tab counts were never re-read after a Status chip value was applied, so the stated mitigation - tab counts computed with the chip already applied, a dead tab reading 0 - is unverified. The one recorded count set (8/7/6/8/2 = 31 = All) is consistent with unfiltered counts.

Dashboard arrival state is not recorded: unknown whether the clicked status lands in the tab row, in the Status chip, or in both, so it is unknown whether the entry path itself starts in a contradicting state.
Date range panel internals were not recorded (presets and direct month/year selection vs month-by-month arrows), so KF-3 could not be checked for this prototype.
Outside-click and Esc dismissal of filter panels were never exercised, so the only known dismissal path for an open panel is unknown.
No filter combination returning zero rows was reached, so the empty state - the message a user sees when the tab/chip conflict does bite - is unknown.
Loading and error states were never observed for any filter control; the state map records no async or failure behaviour.
The interaction between Search and the tab row/Status chip is not recorded: "Changolivia" -> 8 rows does not say whether search respects the active tab or overrides it.
Clear filters was observed as visible on load but never clicked, so it is unknown whether it also wipes the default 90-day range and the status passed in from the Dashboard.
